### 1 — Scene
A mixed meal of leafy salad, cooked meat pieces (likely beef), and rice with cooked vegetables.

### 2 — Vessel
A rounded-square dinner plate, approximately **26 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation:  
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm².**

### 3 — Items
Visible foods include mixed salad leaves, carrot shreds and pale vegetable slices, cooked meat, rice, and cooked vegetables including orange/red pieces and greens. A little glossy sauce appears around the rice and meat; no separate pool of salad dressing is clear.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy
Vegetables are grouped together, excluding the leafy salad. Coverage estimates partition the visible food area to avoid double-counting.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed salad leaves | 38% | 202 cm² × 2.5 cm = 505 ml | 0.15 | 76 g | 20 | 15 kcal |
| Cooked meat, likely beef | 23% | 122 cm² × 1.2 cm = 146 ml | 0.95 | 139 g | 240 | 334 kcal |
| Cooked rice | 15% | 80 cm² × 1.8 cm = 144 ml | 0.8 | 115 g | 130 | 150 kcal |
| Raw and cooked vegetable pieces | 8% | 42 cm² × 1.8 cm = 76 ml | 0.6 | 46 g | 60 | 28 kcal |
| Visible sauce | 1% | 5 cm² × 1 cm = 5 ml | 1.0 | 5 g | 150 | 8 kcal |

**Coverage check:** 38 + 23 + 15 + 8 + 1 = **85%**, consistent with the mostly covered plate. Bulk density is the only allowance for gaps.

### 8 — Sanity check
The estimate is **381 g and approximately 535 kcal**. This is plausible for a plate with a large, light salad and more compact portions of meat and rice. Meat identity and cooking fat are the largest energy uncertainties.
